speaker: Joe Root
quote_text: Hello. Hi James. >> Welcome back as captain for a second stint. How are you feeling about the challenge that lies ahead and returning this test team to winning ways? >> Yeah, I'm really excited um again to get the chance to start heading as well is always nice. Home ground. Um but yeah, there's it's a very talented group of players that are very capable of of special things and um really excited about where we can where we can take this team. How big a rebuilding job is it after what's gone on what's gone on over the last what six months? >> I don't think there's a huge amount that we need to change. I think it's small things that will make a big difference. And it's not about ripping it up. I think it's about keeping a lot of the good stuff that we've been doing for a period of time and that Ben and Baz built for a long a long while. Um but making small adjustments that in game will make a big difference. So, um, giving clarity to the group on what that looks like and, um, and then putting into place over and over again. >> You mentioned Ben and Baz, it's the end of Baz ball. Will you move away from that ultraaggressive style? >> I don't believe that. I don't believe there is a a style where a a one way of playing test cricket. I think you've got to be um adaptable and you you've got to play the situation and the different tempos of the game. You know, it's never the same throughout the five days. There are different challenges and you've got to adjust to the different es and flows of it throughout that period. And ultimately, of course, when you get your opportunity, you want to put teams under pressure and and you want to find ways of driving the game forward, but that might look different in different circumstances. And about it's about recognizing what that looks like. Um, and being skillful and intelligent enough to to execute that at the right times. >> Has it been strange not having been around? It's a big void to fill, isn't it? >> It's a it's a big void to fill and someone that's been ever present for, you know, the best part of 15 years. So, um, clearly it has been different, but again, we've only been together as a a full team for, you know, a day and a half. So, um, you know, I one thing I think that's really important for for all of us is we don't get too stuck in the last six months and we don't get too caught up in the next six months. We've got a very unique series that we find ourselves in. Um and we've got to be very present throughout the whole of it and uh understand the different challenges that um Pakistan present us and and how we can get the best out of ourselves in the conditions we find ourselves in. >> Can you see Ben Stokes returning at a later date? >> Who knows? Who knows? That's a question for Ben. >> Would you try and persuade him? >> I'm looking like I said that's a that's a question for down the line. Um I've just said we need to look after the here and now and that's this series. >> And in the short term Dan Lawrence comes in as that allrounder. Ben Stokes has balanced the team for so long. Is that probably the biggest selection conundrum you've got going forward? It's how you get that balance. >> I think he's trying to find the best team for the right conditions and um you know Dan's been an exceptional player for for Surrey throughout the whole season. His his numbers are amazing. He's he's played some brilliant innings uh and is in great form and I think is a very underrated bowler. Um, so, uh, I think he offers a great amount. Clearly, it is a different, um, makeup to the team and a different balance to things, but there's no reason why that can't be successful either. And it's understanding how we're going to work that through, how we're going to manage that and get the best out of the 11 players that get the opportunity to take the field. >> And you've immediately scrapped the curfew. Just explain. I know you've touched on it, but just just explain why and how you will make sure that the levels of professionalism are maintained without that curfew. What you've said to the guys going forward. >> Yeah, I feel like you want to um you want guys to take responsibility on the field and you have to make sure that they feel that they can um be grown-up adults off it and and take responsibility off it and make good decisions. And ultimately, we've we've got to self police that. We've got to look after ourselves better. we can't find ourselves in a situation like we have done over the last last little while. Um, and everyone knows the responsibilities of of what it takes to play for England. Um, but you know, at the right times, I still think we should be able to celebrate and enjoy that. It's just doing it in the right way. Um, and yeah, just just be grown-ups about it. >> And finally, for me, how close contact have you had with Steven Fleming? How involved has he been with the buildup to this series? >> He's been really good. I've been constant contact with him, speak nearly every day. Um, and yeah, it's it's been good to get to to know him, understand how he works, how he sees things, and and clearly it's going to be very different throughout these three games, but I think very good that, you know, he's he's across things and in constant communication with me and Marcus and we're able to start building on hopefully developing something really strong over the next next little while. Rory, >> do you [clears throat] do you see this challenge now as a as a continuation of what went before with your captain or are you viewing this as a completely blank sheet of paper and sort of a brand new start? >> I think it's very different. Um, if I'm being brutally honest, the landscape's very different. Um, you know, I' I'm a very different player and person that I was when I took over as captain. And I think it's I'm in a very fortunate and unique position where I've got 60 odd games of experience um to look back on and things that I might want to change and do slightly differently. Uh and and then have the time to step away, play in a different environment under a different um a different coach and a different captain and and see the game from a different lens and then be able to mold what I think is the best way of taking this team forward. Um, so in many ways I I I feel as readied as as any other England captain that's ever been before. I've, you know, to have that amount of experience is is invaluable. So, um, yeah, I think it's a completely different set of circumstances. I'm very much looking forward to
